findings.title: REGRESSION (L1): side-wall blade signs cut through the door title signs and lintels, the bracket never reaches the wall, and every side door now carries its name twice
findings.problem:
The L1 fix (19deb71) added a blade sign over each of the three left-wall doors (05 Fabrication Bay, 06 Signal Observatory, 07 Spectrum Delivery). The blade group sits on game.root at world x = s.x+0.95 = -14.05, z = door z (src/hub/lobby.ts:82). Its parts collide with the door's own title plate:
- The grey post box(.06,.5,.06) sits at local x -0.62, which is world x -14.67, y 2.70-3.20.
- The lintel title plate (lobby.ts:92) is at side-wall-local z .30, which is world x about -14.70, y 2.25-2.86.
- So the post runs down through the middle of the title sign. The blade plate (1.7 m wide, 0.48 m tall, y 2.62-3.10, world x -14.90 to -13.20) also crosses the lintel rbox (world x -15.0 to -14.72, y 2.42-2.68) and the title plate.

On screen the post spears 'Signal Observatory' (lobby-models-18), the blade plate covers half of 'Fabrication Bay' (lobby-models-16, -44, -46), and from inside the room the post crosses the '05' digits (lobby-models-47).

The bracket also doesn't touch the wall. The wall face is at world x -14.875, the arm box(1.3,…) ends at local -0.65 (world -14.70) and the post is at -14.67, so the whole sign hangs about 17 cm off the wall (DR-72).

The plate is a single-sided MeshBasicMaterial facing world +z, so from the -z side it disappears and leaves a bare grey L-bracket. Each side door now shows its name twice ('05 · Fabrication Bay' on the blade, 'Fabrication Bay' on the lintel), which goes against DR-41's one-value-once rule.

This is the first thing a player sees on the left wall, and it reads as broken signage. It's a regression of the L1 fix listed in the re-check list.
findings.fix:
Rebuild the blade in src/hub/lobby.ts:82:
1. Parent it to kit.side, the side wall's inside group, at wall-local (lx=-s.z, 0, 0). That way it also folds with the cutaway (see the next finding).
2. Drop the vertical post.
3. Add an arm part(blade, box(.05,.05,1.5), metal, 0, 2.95, .75) that starts at local z 0, on the wall face, and runs out to z 1.5. Keep it under the cap, whose underside is at y 3.0.
4. Hang two plates back to back from the arm: signPlate(…, width 1.0, h 72) at local (±.004, 2.68, .95) with rotation.y = ±π/2. They span z .45-1.45 and y 2.54-2.82, so they clear the lintel front (z .28) and the title plate (z .30).
5. Delete the lintel title plate on side doors (keep it on back doors), or shorten the blade text to the number only ('05'), so the name appears once.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/lobby-models/a.mjs and d.mjs and retake lobby-models-16, -18, -44, -46 and -47. No grey post may cross a title. Both blade faces read from ±z orbits. The bracket touches the wall in a 90° orbit close-up. g.audit(.02) stays [].
findings.verify_reason: I checked the geometry at src/hub/lobby.ts:82 and :92. The blade group sits on g.root at world x -14.05. Its post is at world x -14.70..-14.64, y 2.70-3.20, directly in front of the title plate (world x -14.70, y 2.255-2.865). The blade plate (x -14.90..-13.20, y 2.62-3.10, plane z=s.z+.03) cuts through both the title plate and the lintel (y 2.42-2.68). Screenshots match. lobby-models-16 shows the post spearing 'Signal Observatory' and 'Spectrum Delivery', and the blade covering 'Fabrication Bay'. lobby-models-18 and -47 show the post crossing '05'. My own -z orbit (verify-lobby-models-06, -07) shows that from behind, the single-sided plate is culled and only a bare grey L-bracket is left. Two corrections. First, the plate itself reaches x -14.90, past the wall face at -14.875, so it is the arm and post that hang about 17 cm off the wall, not the whole sign. Second, DR-41 is about HUD panels; the duplicated name is mild redundancy, not a DR-41 breach. It is still a visible regression of the L1 fix.
extra_evidence: src/levels/decor.ts:35-37 (the inside group's origin is the wall centre line; its +z face is at .125)
findings.fix_correction: The proposed rebuild is geometrically sound. With kit.side local z pointing into the room, rotation.y=±π/2 plates face ±world z, sit at z .45-1.45 and clear the lintel (.28) and the title plate (.30). The bottom at y 2.54 also clears the leaf top (2.27). One detail: the arm starts at local z 0, the wall centre, so 12.5 cm of it is buried in the wall. That's fine, but say it's intentional. Prefer step 5's option of keeping the lintel name and putting only the number on the blade, because the lintel sign is what shows on the door-approach view.

findings.title: Blade signs and lit wing-lamp glows live on game.root, so they float in mid-air when the wall cuts away
findings.problem:
Shell walls fold to 0.9 m stubs when the camera swings behind them (src/game.ts:384-385). The doors are children of the folding upper group, so they vanish correctly (lobby-models-04).

Two things are not children of that group:
- the side-door blade signs, built with group(g.root, …) at src/hub/lobby.ts:82;
- the lit-lamp glow sprites, built with glow(g.root, …) at lobby.ts:97.

When the player orbits west (camera on the -x side) the left wall drops, but the 1.3 m grey blade bracket stays hanging at y 2.7-3.2 right in front of the camera (lobby-models-45: a large grey L-shaped pipe in the foreground, with its single-sided plate culled). The same applies to every lit wing glow once a job is done: the sprites keep floating at y 3.35 over a wall that is no longer there. That breaks DR-75 (cutaway must not leave artefacts) and DR-72 (nothing floats), and it appears on a common orbit in the hub.
findings.fix: Parent the blade to kit.side (wall-local coordinates; see the previous finding). Parent the glow to the door frame group f: glow(f, …, 1.4, .35).position.set(0, lampY, .25). Both then scale with wall.group and hide when scale.y < .03. Give the sprite a lower size (see the wing-lamp finding).
findings.verify: Use a done-state lobby (localStorage best for playground and qfn, as in tools/lobby-models/d.mjs). Orbit +262 and +524 and retake lobby-models-45 and a 180° done-state shot. No bracket or glow should remain above a stubbed wall.
findings.verify_reason: Code: the blade is on g.root (lobby.ts:82) and the done glow is on g.root at a world position (lobby.ts:97). The cutaway only scales and hides wall.group, the upper group (src/game.ts:385-386). I reproduced it with a done-state lobby (playground, meeting and qfn bests). In verify-lobby-models-10 the back wall is cut away and two lit glows float in mid-air over the floor where the wall was. In verify-lobby-models-11 the side wall is cut away, and three bare grey blade brackets plus the qfn glow hang beside Pip. lobby-models-45 shows the same bracket in the foreground. I lowered the priority to P2: this is a cosmetic artefact on orbit, it doesn't block or mislead play, and the glow part only appears after jobs are done. DR-72 applies directly. DR-75 is only loosely related.

findings.title: Door leaves swing out into the lobby through Pip (no collider, outward arc 1.66 m, the approach point inside the arc)
findings.problem:
Every job door opens on a spring when Pip comes within 2.6 m: d.leaf.rotation.y = -d.open*1.25 (src/hub/lobby.ts:130). The leaf (rbox 1.66×2.26, lobby.ts:90) is hinged at frame-local x -0.84, and the negative rotation swings it out into the lobby (+z).

The door's interaction point is at = door + 1.1 m (lobby.ts:77-78). It sits 0.84 m across and about 0.96 m out from the hinge, about 1.28 m away, which is inside the leaf's 1.66 m sweep. At intermediate angles near 0.9 rad the leaf passes straight through Pip's centre. At full open (1.25 rad) its line is still only 0.43 m from his centre.

The leaf has no collider, so in every 'Enter' shot it cuts through Pip's arm, back or hat:
- lobby-models-13: the leaf is at Pip's left arm.
- lobby-models-14: the leaf is behind and through Pip.
- lobby-models-18: the leaf passes through the hat.
- lobby-models-22: the leaf cuts Pip's right side.

This is the moment the hub is about, walking up to a door, and Pip clips through the leaf every time. It breaks DR-70 (nothing interpenetrates) and the spirit of DR-73 (nothing passes through Pip). The leaf's back face is also a blank white slab: no colour panel, number or knob (lobby-models-14, DR-63).
findings.fix:
Pick one of these in src/hub/lobby.ts:
- **(a) Swing inward:** change :130 to d.leaf.rotation.y=+d.open*1.25. The leaf turns behind the opaque portal plane (z .05) and into the wall box, so it simply disappears into the corridor. That's the reading you want, and nothing sweeps the lobby. Optionally draw a leaf silhouette on the corridor's hinge-side wall in portal.ts's side-wall branch: darken where h.z > -1.66 and the hinge side matches.
- **(b) Barn door:** keep rotation 0. Slide d.leaf.position.x = -.84 + d.open*1.75. Move the leaf to z .19 so it clears the post fronts at z .13, and add a rail box(3.8,.06,.06) at (0.9, 2.36, .2).

With either option, also mirror the colour panel, the number plate and a second knob onto the leaf's -z face (DR-63). For example, part(leaf, box(1.3,.9,.02), toon(color), .83, 1.55, -.03) plus a signPlate rotated π.
findings.verify: Rerun a.mjs and b.mjs and retake lobby-models-13, -14, -18 and -22. Pip's silhouette must be unbroken by the leaf. Also add a spec that walks to each door.at from both sides and checks that the leaf's world bounding box never intersects a 0.36 m sphere at Pip.
findings.verify_reason: Code: the leaf hinge is at frame-local x -.84. rotation.y=-open*1.25 swings it into +z, out into the lobby (lobby.ts:130). It has no solid(). For Lunch the hinge is at world (-3.16, -9.76) and door.at is (-2.32, -8.9), 1.20 m from the hinge and inside the 1.66 m sweep. At full open the leaf line is about 0.53 m from Pip's centre (the finding says 0.43), close to his arm. I reproduced a clean interpenetration. In verify-lobby-models-08 Pip walks along the wall from the hinge side to (-7.50, -8.55) at the Big Meeting door, and the open leaf slices vertically through the middle of his body. lobby-models-13 and verify-lobby-models-04 show the leaf at or over his left arm. The blank white back face is confirmed in lobby-models-14.
findings.fix_correction: Option (a), swinging inward, isn't clean. A 1.66 m leaf turned +1.25 rad ends about 1.2 m behind the wall's back face, in the void outside the room. With the camera pitched up (pitch clamps to 1.25 rad) the leaf tops show above and behind the 3 m wall cap. Either clamp the inward swing to about 0.35 rad (the opaque portal already reads as 'open'), or hide the leaf when open > .3. Option (b), the barn door, also needs adjusting. A leaf at frame-local z .15-.23 collides with the medal at z .18 (x .91-1.25), so move the medal (finding 7). The rail at y 2.33-2.39, z .2 would cross the lower 6-12 cm of the lintel title plate, which hangs down to y 2.255 at z .16. Shrink or raise the title plate so its bottom is above 2.40 (for example h 64, centred at 2.66), or hang the rail behind the plate. Keep the spec idea: leaf world bounding box vs a 0.36 m sphere at Pip, approached from both sides.

findings.title: Directory board: rows overlap by 11.5 cm and z-fight, it floats with no stand, reads in zig-zag order, and shrinks the text unevenly
findings.problem:
The directory board behind reception (src/hub/lobby.ts:59-60) is a box(3.3, h, .08) INK slab whose bottom is at y 1.25. It has no stand, no legs and no collider. It sits 6 cm behind and 19 cm above the desk's back edge; the desk top rbox(4.1, .08, 1.2) is at y 1.02 and covers z -1.2 to 0, while the board is at z -1.3. From the side it plainly hangs in the air (lobby-models-33, DR-72).

The nine plates overlap:
- signPlate width 1.5 with h 64 and w 256 gives plates 0.375 m tall.
- The rows are spaced 0.26 m apart, so each plate overlaps the next by 0.115 m (31%).
- All of them sit at the same z (.05).

The rounded transparent margins therefore fight in depth, which shows as dotted jagged seams between rows. Look at '01 Big Meeting' and '03 Overheating Arcade' in lobby-models-09 and -12, and every row in lobby-models-10 and -34 (title screen). This breaks DR-70 and DR-77.

The layout uses i%2 for the column, so the reading order zig-zags: the left column is 00, 02, 03R, 05, 07 and the right is 01, 03, 04, 06. labelTexture also shrinks each label to fit (src/render/labels.ts:9-10), so '03 Overheating Arcade' renders at about half the cap height of '01 Big Meeting'. At the game camera every row is under 8 px (lobby-models-01; DR-48).

The board is the hub's centrepiece, and it currently reads as a glitchy TV.
findings.fix:
In src/hub/lobby.ts:59-60:
1. Lay the plates out column-major: col = i < rows ? 0 : 1 and row = i % rows.
2. Make each plate 1.45 wide with h 44, giving 0.25 m, and set the row pitch to 0.29 m. Then h = .3 + rows*.29 = 1.75.
3. Stagger z by row (.05 + row*.0015) so no two plates share a plane.
4. Give labelTexture a fixed `size` option (add `size?:number` to its options in labels.ts and skip the shrink loop when it is set). Use the smallest fitted size across all nine titles so every row has the same cap height.
5. Add a stand: two posts part(board, box(.08,1.3,.08), toon(DMETAL), ±1.5, .65, -.02) from the floor to the board bottom, a 4 cm wood frame rbox(3.42, h+.12, .06, .03) in '#c98a55' behind the INK panel at z -.03, and solid(g, 3.4, h, .12, 0, 1.25+h/2, -1.3).
findings.verify: Retake lobby-models-09, -10, -12, -33 (side view) and -34. There must be no dotted seams between rows, legs must reach the floor, and the rows must read top to bottom 00…04, then 05…07. Run g.audit(.02) with the new collider.
findings.verify_reason: Code (lobby.ts:59-60): each plate is 1.5*64/256 = 0.375 m tall on a 0.26 m pitch, so neighbours overlap by 0.115 m, all at the same z of .05. Columns are chosen by i%2, so the layout zig-zags: left 00, 02, 03R, 05, 07 and right 01, 03, 04, 06. There's no stand or collider, and the board bottom is at 1.25, 19 cm above the desk top and 6 cm behind its back edge. The labelTexture shrink loop is at labels.ts:9. lobby-models-09 clearly shows the dotted seams (01/03, 03/04) and '03 Overheating Arcade' at a visibly smaller cap height. I lowered the priority to P2: these are z-fighting and overlap visual bugs (DR-77 is P2). The doors carry the same names, so the directory's information isn't lost.
findings.fix_correction: With the new pitch the board becomes 1.75 m tall, with its top at 3.0 m. That makes the occlusion in finding 4 worse, so the fade fix from finding 4 must land at the same time, or lower the bottom to 1.15 and use a 0.27 pitch. Also use w 512 / h 88 instead of 256 / 44, because a 44 px-tall canvas renders the text blurry at zoom 9. The stand posts at local z -.02 (world -1.32) clear the desk back face (-1.15), so that's fine.

findings.title: The 3.3 × 1.6 m directory board hides Pip completely and is not an occluder; Pip's head also passes through it
findings.problem:
The board (src/hub/lobby.ts:59) is opaque, 3.3 m wide and reaches 2.85 m. It isn't pushed into game.occluders, so the fade in src/game.ts:386-388 never touches it.

After a 180° orbit near reception, Pip stands on the desk side and disappears entirely behind the black slab (lobby-models-11). Only the 'Grab the mug' prompt shows he is there. The same happens from the default camera whenever Pip walks the aisle behind reception.

The board also has no collider and its bottom is at 1.25 m. Pip is about 1.76 m tall, so walking behind the desk at z ≈ -1.3 puts his head through the board.

This breaks DR-12 (the camera never hides Pip, and a mesh over 1.2 m fades) and DR-70.
findings.fix: In lobby.ts:59, build the board panel with a cloned transparent material: const m = toon(INK).clone(); m.transparent = true. Parent it to g.root instead of decorRoot, because freeze() would merge it, and push the mesh into g.occluders, the same pattern interiorWall uses at decor.ts:44-49. Add solid(g, 3.4, 1.7, .12, 0, 2.05, -1.3) so Pip can't walk his head through it. Also fade the plates: give them depthWrite false and add them to occluders.
findings.verify: Rerun a.mjs step '11-board-back'. Pip must be visible (more than 70% of his pixels) through a faded board. Add a DR-12 sweep at zoom 9 and 38 with Pip at (0, -1.8).
findings.verify_reason: The board is in decorRoot and is not pushed to game.occluders (lobby.ts:59; fade loop at game.ts:387-388). I reproduced it at the default camera with no orbit. Pip walked to (-0.29, -1.77) behind reception and is completely hidden by the board (verify-lobby-models-01; only the prompt-less scene is visible). lobby-models-11 shows the 180° case. Head through the board: Pip can stand at z -1.51 (stopped by the desk collider); the board is at z -1.30 and his body radius is 0.36. In verify-lobby-models-02 his hat pokes through the board's plates. This breaks DR-12, which is P1.
findings.fix_correction: The proposed solid at z -1.3 (depth .12) leaves Pip about 0.36-0.5 m behind the board, still fully hidden at the default camera, so the fade is the essential part. The ray in game.ts:387 aims only at p.y+.4. Check that this ray actually hits the board when Pip's head is the only part behind it (DR-12 notes the single-ray limitation).

findings.title: Reception desk and board have bare backs, and the desk 'monitors' are plain ink cubes that read as speakers
findings.problem:
Reception is the lobby's only big fixture, but it has fewer than 6 cues and large flat faces. That fails DR-62 (stations and fixtures show at least 6 cues; no plain face over 0.5 m²) and DR-63 (finished backs, because the player orbits):
- The desk body rbox(4,1,1.1) has a 4 m² featureless cream back and two plain 1.1 m² ends (src/hub/lobby.ts:55; lobby-models-11, -33).
- The board's back is a 5.3 m² flat black slab (lobby-models-04, -11).
- The two 'screens' are rbox(.5,.35,.4) in INK at (±1.2, 1.25, -0.1) (lobby.ts:57). They have no bezel, no screen face and no stand, and from the front they read as two black speaker cubes (lobby-models-09, -12).
- There is no receptionist chair behind the desk, and no bell, phone, keyboard or papers, so the receptionist blob at (-1.4, 0.6) stands in front of the desk rather than behind it.
findings.fix:
In lobby.ts:55-57:
- Replace the INK cubes with makeProp('monitor', INK, 2), rotated π so the screens face the staff side at z -1.0. The kit monitor has a bezel, screen and stand (src/props/prefabs.ts monitor case). Add a lit back-panel decal so the camera side shows a logo.
- On the staff side, add a kick panel and two drawer pedestals: rbox(.5,.7,.5,.05) in '#e9dcc4' at (±1.3, .36, -1.05) with ink pulls box(.2,.03,.02).
- Add a task chair, makeProp('chair', '#5ED6CC'), at (0.4, 0, -1.6).
- Put a bell (cyl .08 plus sphere), a phone rbox and a paper stack on the top at y 1.07.
- On the desk ends, add a teal stripe box(.04,.5,1.0).
- Cover the board back with a cork texture, wallArt(board,'cork',…) rotated π, or add vent slots and a 'CIRCUIT CREW' logo decal.
- Move the receptionist NPC to (-.8, -1.7), facing +z (src/levels/lobby.ts:10).
findings.verify: Take zoom-9 shots of reception from the front (a.mjs '09') and the back (orbit 524, '11'). List at least 6 cues and no plain face over 0.5 m². The monitors must read as monitors in a first-look test.
findings.verify_reason: Code: the desk is a plain cream rbox (lobby.ts:55), and the 'monitors' are INK rbox(.5,.35,.4) cubes with no bezel or stand (lobby.ts:57). The receptionist NPC is at (-1.4, .6) (src/levels/lobby.ts:10), in front of the desk, whose collider spans z -1.15..-0.05. Screenshots: lobby-models-09 and verify-lobby-models-14 show black cubes, lobby-models-11 a bare cream back and a flat black board back. I lowered the priority to P2 because this is model detail with no effect on play or teaching. makeProp('monitor') and 'chair' exist (prefabs.ts:66, :77).
findings.fix_correction: Don't move the receptionist to (-.8, -1.7). As verify-lobby-models-01 proves, anything standing at z ≈ -1.7 is fully hidden by the opaque board at the default camera. It would also sit about 0.4 m from a board that has no collider. Either land finding 4's fade first, or keep the NPC in front of the desk and only add the chair and drawers behind it.

findings.title: The 'wing lights up' reward lamp is a grey ball on top of the wall cap, nearly off the top of the frame at the default camera, with its fixture upside down
findings.fix:
Make the lamp a wall sconce over the lintel, below the cap (src/hub/lobby.ts:96-97):
- Mount a backplate rbox(.3,.2,.04) at frame-local (0, 2.95, .02).
- Add an arm box(.05,.05,.18) at (0, 2.95, .1).
- Hang a downward cone shade, CylinderGeometry(.07,.16,.14) in the wing colour, at (0, 2.9, .2).
- Put the bulb sphere(.07) at (0, 2.85, .2).
- Add a done-state light strip along the underside of the lintel: box(1.9,.04,.03) at (0, 2.41, .15), hot(color, 1.6) when done and toon('#8a8fa6') otherwise.
- Make the glow glow(f, …, .45, .35) at (0, 2.85, .3), which is under 1.5× the source.
- Optionally tint the wainscot rail segment under a done door with the wing colour.

The lit lamp and strip then sit about 60-80 px lower on screen and read at the default camera.
findings.verify: Rerun b.mjs, then retake lobby-models-19 and -21 and crop the top 260 px (d.mjs '43'). Every lit wing must be fully inside the frame at the default camera, and unlit vs lit must be tellable in greyscale.
findings.verify_reason: Code (lobby.ts:96-97): the bulb is sphere r .13 at y 3.35 (3.22-3.48), with its socket cylinder above it at 3.44-3.56. The cap top is 3.18 (decor.ts:37), so the bulb hovers about 4 cm above the cap and the socket is attached to nothing. The glow is 1.4 m against a 0.26 m bulb, 5.4×, which breaks DR-66's 1.5× limit. Screenshots: lobby-models-01 and -43 show grey balls on the cap. In lobby-models-19 the lit glows sit at y ≈ 0-25 px and are cut by the top edge. The lamp is the only in-world progress cue ('Light every wing' bonus), so P1 stands.
findings.fix_correction: The proposed sconce and strip collide with the door title plate. That plate is at frame-local z .16 and spans y 2.255-2.865, x ±.975, and it hangs below the lintel. The shade (y 2.83-2.97, z .04-.36) and bulb (y 2.78-2.92, z .2) at x 0 overlap its top edge and sit in front of the text. The light strip at y 2.39-2.43, z .135-.165 runs through the plate's lower part. The backplate at y 2.85-3.05 also enters the cap, which starts at 3.0. Instead, mount the sconce beside the lintel (frame-local x ±1.3, y 2.75, backplate at z .02, below the 3.0 cap). Put the done-state light on the post fronts: box(.06,2.2,.02) at (±.95, 1.2, .14), hot(color) when done. Glow ≤ .4 m.

findings.title: The best-grade medal hangs half off the frame post, 18 cm in front of the wallpaper, and is about 12 px at the game camera
findings.problem:
The medal is signPlate(f, best.grade, 1.08, 2.12, .18, .34, …) (src/hub/lobby.ts:94):
- Its centre x 1.08 is past the frame post's outer edge (1.06), so half of the 0.34 m badge overhangs empty air.
- It sits at frame-local z .18, while the wallpaper face is at about frame-local z .006, so it floats about 17 cm proud of the wall. At an oblique orbit it visibly hovers beside the door (lobby-models-20, -21, -47; DR-72 wants 0.5-1 cm).
- At the game camera it's a 10-12 px chip, and the grey 'B'/'C' variant on '#dfe3ea' melts into the cream wall (lobby-models-19). DR-47 and DR-48 call for a state readable at the game camera.
findings.fix:
Mount the medal on the lintel's title sign as a rosette:
- rbox(.46,.46,.04,.1) in the medal colour (A '#ffc629', B '#c7ccd6', C '#c98a55') at frame-local (0.98, 2.56, .2), overlapping the sign's right end.
- The grade plate at z .225, width .4.
- Two ribbon tails: box(.08,.18,.01) at (±.06, 2.3, .2), rotated ±.2.

Or put it on the leaf's colour panel at leaf-local (1.35, 1.55, .085). Use INK text on all medals for contrast.
findings.verify: Retake lobby-models-20 and a 90° orbit close-up. The medal must touch its mount, be at least 20 px at the default camera (lobby-models-19), and read A/B/C in greyscale.
findings.verify_reason: Code (lobby.ts:94): the medal is centred at x 1.08 with width .34, so it spans .91-1.25. The post runs .84-1.06, so about 56% of the badge overhangs. It sits at z .18, about 5 cm in front of the post face and about 17 cm in front of the wallpaper (frame-local ≈ .006). lobby-models-20 and -47 show the A/B badge hanging off the post edge; in -19 it's a roughly 12 px chip. P2 is correct.
findings.fix_correction: If finding 2's barn-door option is chosen, the ribbon tails at y 2.21-2.39, z .2 overlap the sliding leaf (top 2.27, z .15-.23). Drop the tails or put the rosette at y ≥ 2.45.

findings.title: The lobby beanbag still reads as a lilac macaron or a lying coworker: two stacked even lobes in BLOBC purple, the same hue as the receptionist
findings.problem:
The beanbag at (8.6, 5.8) is coloured '#b392f0' (src/levels/lobby.ts:7), which is exactly BLOBC[0] (src/render/kit.ts:9) and the receptionist blob's purple. findings.title: Workshop arch: decor blocks pass through the bench leg and have no colliders, the arch is a dead end Pip gets wedged in, its two signs z-fight, and it has no 'workshop' identity
findings.problem:
The Workshop arch (src/hub/lobby.ts:100-105) is anchored at (7.5, 4.3). The atrium bench is at (6.5, 3.6), spanning x 5.5-7.5 and z 3.3-3.9 (lobby.ts:63), directly behind the arch.

- The blocks have no colliders. Pip walked into them at (7.0, 4.25): his 0.36 m ball reaches z 3.89, inside the blocks (lobby-models-40).

**Identity.** Beyond the two signs, the arch is two teal posts, a lintel, a cream floor tile and three toy blocks. Nothing says 'workshop' or 'practice bench' (no tools, pegboard, vice, mini bench or screen). That's under DR-62's 6-cue minimum for a fixture.

Rules broken: DR-70, DR-77, DR-62, DR-16.
findings.fix:
1. Move the right atrium bench in lobby.ts:63 from (6.5, 3.6) to (4.6, 3.6), or rotate it 90° to (5.2, 4.6), so the arch has at least 1.5 m of clear floor behind it.
2. Delete the three loose blocks.
3. Behind the arch, add a small practice bench: rbox(1.6,.08,.7) top at y .9 on two legs, with solid(g, 1.6, .95, .7, 7.5, .47, 3.4).
4. Hang a pegboard on the arch's back face: box(2,.9,.04) in '#d9c3a0' with hole decals, plus a spanner, a screwdriver and a mini reel as kit parts (cyl and box).

findings.verify:

The blocks have no colliders: in verify-lobby-models-13 Pip walks to (8.0, 3.5) and his boot is inside the teal block. The purple block overlaps the bench leg by only about 3 cm (x 7.32-7.35). I refuted the 'dead end'. A walk straight down the centre (x 7.5) stops at z 4.245 against the bench, but a walk at x 7.95 passes through to z 2.19 (verify-lobby-models-12 run), so the arch is half-blocked rather than a dead end. findings.title: Locked door: the 'LOCKED' plate sits at Pip's chest height and is hidden whenever he walks up, and the padlock is a plain job-yellow cube

findings.title: Door name signs auto-shrink, so long names ('Overheating Arcade', 'Cable Playground') render at half the cap height of short ones and fall to about 6 px at the game camera
findings.problem:

The hub's only job is choosing a door, and half the door names are below DR-48's 14 px. The row looks uneven, as if the signs were different sizes.

Widen the lintel sign to 2.1 m with w 320, h 96, and let long names break onto two lines ('Overheating / Arcade') at the same size. Raise the lintel's rbox to 2.3 m wide so the sign stays mounted.

findings.title: Phone survey (Tab) shows 3 of the 9 doors: the hub's whole purpose (choose a door) is cropped on portrait screens
findings.problem:
Survey zoom is a fixed 44 (src/game.ts:366). At 390×844, the lobby survey frames only Big Meeting, Lunch Rush and Overheating Arcade, plus reception (lobby-models-42). Cable Playground, Arcade Rush, Robot Garage and all three side doors are off-screen. The phone start shot shows two and a half doors (lobby-models-41).

At 1440×900 the survey does show all nine (lobby-models-02). This breaks DR-21 (the survey shows the whole room on a phone in portrait), and in the hub the survey is the door picker's overview.
findings.fix: In src/game.ts:366, make the survey distance fit the room: zoom = max(44, (max(level.width, level.depth/ cam.aspect)*0.5)/tan(fov/2)/cos(pitch)*1.1). For the 30 m lobby at aspect 0.46 that's roughly 75-80. Also set the survey pitch to about 1.0 in portrait, so the board reads top-down.
findings.verify: Rerun c.mjs's phone block and retake lobby-models-42. All 9 door frames are visible.
findings.verify_reason: The survey zoom is a fixed 44 (game.ts:366). lobby-models-42 (390×844) shows only Big Meeting, Lunch Rush and Overheating Arcade; lobby-models-02 (1440×900) shows all nine. DR-21 is P1 playability, and on a phone the hub's survey is the door overview.
findings.fix_correction: The formula has width and depth swapped. The room width must fit the horizontal FOV: dist = max((depth/2)/tan(vfov/2), (width/2)/(tan(vfov/2)*aspect)) * 1.1, then divide out lensScale(fov) (game.ts:376), since that scale is applied afterwards. For the 30 m lobby at aspect .46 this comes out at about 90, not 75-80, depending on fov. Clamp it to the camera far plane.

findings.title: About 590 draw calls for a 15-prop hub (693 in survey): doors, signs and portals are on game.root and never merged
findings.problem:
snap().drawCalls is 592 at the lobby start and 693 in the survey. The Playground has 109 props and 782 (all measured with fullfx at 1440×900).

The causes:
- Doors are built on the shell walls' upper groups (game.root), so freeze(decorRoot) (src/game.ts:105) never merges them.
- Each door has about 15 meshes, plus 3-5 signPlate meshes, each with its own MeshBasicMaterial (src/render/labels.ts:16).
- There are 9 board plates and 9 portal ShaderMaterials.
- Blade signs and lamps are also unmerged.

The fps is 60 on the host GPU, but DR-24 caps draw calls at about 250. A hub with this little in it should be the cheapest scene, and it leaves no headroom for the density fix above.
findings.fix:
1. In Lobby.door() (src/hub/lobby.ts:76-98), split the static parts from the moving ones. Static parts are the frame posts, lintel, threshold, title sign and medal; moving ones are the leaf, portal, spill and lamp. Merge the static parts per wall with mergeGeometries into one mesh per material, parented to the wall's upper group so they still fold.
2. Build the lintel sign textures into one canvas atlas per wall, so there's one MeshBasicMaterial per wall.
3. Draw the 9 board plates into a single canvas texture on one plane.
findings.verify: Rerun a.mjs. snap().drawCalls at start must be ≤ 250 with the same visuals. lobby.spec.ts must still pass.
findings.verify_reason: My run gave snap().drawCalls of 592 at start and 670 in the survey (the finding says 693) at 60 fps. Doors are parented to kit.back and kit.side, which are on g.root, so freeze(decorRoot) (game.ts:105) never merges them. Each signPlate has its own MeshBasicMaterial (labels.ts:15). Note that drawCalls counts every pass, composer and outlines included (game.ts:450), so there are about half as many meshes. It is still above the DR-24 budget of about 250 under the same counting method.
extra_evidence: verify v1.mjs output: props 15, dc 592, survey dc 670, fps 60

findings.title: Seen at a grazing angle, the open portal reads as a shallow orange closet, and the destination view vanishes
findings.problem: The interior-mapped doorway (src/render/portal.ts) works well from the front: lobby-models-13, -18 and -22 show a corridor and the destination thumbnail. From an orbit of about 35° (lobby-models-14), the ray mostly hits the corridor's side wall (uDepth 2.8, lobby.ts:86). The opening becomes a flat wing-colour grid of panels and the destination image disappears. The panel pattern, step(.06,fract(h.z*1.4)) (portal.ts:43-44), is evenly spaced with no perspective cue, so the corridor looks like a coloured wall stuck inside the frame. The portal also has no lit floor seam at the threshold, so its base doesn't connect to the lobby floor at oblique angles.
findings.fix:
In portal.ts's side-wall branch:
- Darken the walls with depth more strongly, for example col *= mix(1.0, .55, depth).
- Add a skirting line (step(.1, h.y+half_.y)) and a few wall-lamp dots, so the corridor reads as a hallway.
- Shorten uDepth to 2.0 in lobby.ts:86 so the far room stays in view from wider angles.

notes.models:
Lobby models get mixed marks. What works:
- The doors are the strongest fixtures in the game's hubs: chunky wing-coloured frames, a glossy leaf with a colour panel, number plate, knob and threshold, and an interior-mapped portal that shows a real corridor with the destination room at its end when you look at it from the front (lobby-models-13, -18, -22).
- The shell walls (wainscot, rail, wallpaper, thick cap) and the wood plank floor (median luma 181) read well. Outlines are present, and Pip's darkest pixels are about luma 49.
- The chairs (5-star base, armrests) and kraft boxes (tape, flap seam, label) pass the squint test.
- g.audit(.02) returns []. That's only because most broken parts are decor without colliders.

What's wrong:
- The side-door blade signs added for L1 now cut through the door titles and lintels, hang off the wall, and float after the cutaway.
- Door leaves swing out through Pip.
- The directory board is a floating, collider-less, non-fading black slab whose plates overlap and z-fight.
- The 'wing lights up' lamps sit on top of the wall, almost out of frame.
- The medal floats 17 cm off the wall.
- The Workshop arch is a dead end with blocks clipping the bench.
- The beanbag still reads as a lilac macaron or coworker.
- The cooler and reception lack detail, and the pendants hang from the sky.

At game camera most props are detailed enough. At close-up the reception and Workshop fall under DR-62's 6 cues.
notes.fun: As a hub the lobby has no fail state and needs none, but there is very little physical fun. There are 15 props in a 600 m² room. A plant and a coworker get knocked over when you walk into them, and that's the only slapstick (the plant at (-5,-1.2) toppled on a straight walk to a door, visible lying in lobby-models-27 to -29). There's no cable anywhere, so the game's star mechanic is missing from the first walkable room (DR-05). The meta goals ('Light every wing', medals) are the hub's reward loop, but the lamps that show them are nearly off-screen and the medals are tiny, so finishing a job doesn't change the lobby in a way the player notices. Making progress physical and visible at the default camera, plus a small plug-in toy at reception, would make returning to the hub feel rewarding.
notes.playability:
Doors work. Walking to a door's `at` point opens it with a nice spring, the prompt names the job, and E enters. The locked Rush door gives a clear prompt and a rattle. Zero console or page errors across the four scripts (start, survey, orbits, done state, norim, phone, title). The problems:
- The directory board hides Pip completely on a 180° orbit and Pip's head passes through it (DR-12).
- The Workshop arch invites walking through but traps Pip against the bench at (7.0,4.25).
- On a phone, the survey shows only 3 of 9 doors (DR-21).
- About 592 draw calls for 15 props (DR-24).
- Scripted straight walks also stalled against the desk (to (0,-5.6)), which hints that the desk plus board block a natural line toward the middle back doors. A human will walk round, but a clutter-free aisle should exist.
notes.teaching: The lobby teaches no electronics by design: it's a hub with no fail state. The only teaching-adjacent elements are the job order on the directory board (which reads in zig-zag order, 00/02/03R… then 01/03/04…, so it doesn't convey a progression) and the lock on Arcade Rush ('finish 03 first'), which communicates the order well through the prompt, though the on-door LOCKED plate is hidden behind Pip. A lit wing-colour lamp strip per completed job, plus a reception 'plug the lamp' toy, would let the hub reinforce the core loop-and-switch idea without text.
notes.clarity: Door titles are readable at zoom 9 to 18, but they auto-shrink: 'Overheating Arcade' and 'Cable Playground' render at about half the cap height of 'Lunch Rush', about 6 px at the default camera. Side doors carry their name twice. The objective marker is a small pale triangle, about 14 to 18 px, above the next door's number plate (lobby-models-01, -43). It points correctly but is easy to miss (DR-44). The first frame shows only the six back doors: the side doors are cut off or under the job card. The Workshop uses 'practise' while the code and URL use 'practice', and the HUD stays live behind its picker. At spawn there's no misleading prompt (L2 improved), but at reception the only prompt is 'Grab the mug' for a stray floor mug.
